ec28e8b719.q: What safety changes did Targa Tasmania implement after the 2024 coroner's report on fatalities?
ec28e8b719.a: The coroner's report contained 90 recommendations. Mark Perry stated they implemented many of these recommendations, though they believed some went too far while others didn't go far enough. The changes included the Targa Academy, speed limits, and modifications to course setup. Notably, the 2024 event was the first where no medical intervention vehicle had to enter a live stage to attend to a competitor.

11a31de296.q: Why did Targa Tasmania move from April/May to November scheduling after 2024?
11a31de296.a: The event moved to November to keep the event on dry roads, which theoretically should make the event safer. November offered daylight savings and better weather. However, the move created unexpected challenges: more tourists, cruise ships, and traffic on the island in November caused significantly more disruption from road closures compared to the traditionally quiet April/May period.

87512a6384.q: How many years was Targa Tasmania unable to run events due to COVID-19 restrictions?
87512a6384.a: During the two-year COVID period, Targa only lost one event in 2020 (Targa Tasmania in Tasmania proper, due to island border closures). Despite this, Targa High Country and Targa Barrier Reef continued operating. Competitors from other states quarantined for two weeks in Queensland and another two weeks upon return home just to compete in the three-day event, demonstrating dedication to the Targa family.

d980e5e1b8.q: When did Mark Perry become CEO of Targa Tasmania and what was his mandate?
d980e5e1b8.a: Mark Perry became CEO in 2006 under Octagon management. At that time, entry numbers were declining and the 15th anniversary event had been smaller than hoped. Octagon essentially gave him an ultimatum: turn the event around within two years or it would be closed. Perry successfully stabilized and grew the event, expanding it from a single Tasmania event to multiple events including Targa High Country, Targa West Point, and Targa Adelaide.

6c20f4ba49.q: What apprenticeship trades does the Modern Classic Car Foundation offer to young people?
6c20f4ba49.a: The Modern Classic Car Foundation currently offers training in four main trades: paint and panel work, live vehicle mechanics, auto electrical work, and trimming. They are also working to establish engine machining training, which has been difficult to set up, and plan to add motorbike training later in the year. Apprentices are employed by the foundation, attend standard TAFE training, and work in a 'man and boy' mentorship scheme where they are paired with experienced tradespeople.
